    AI Overview
    The 130th Boston Marathon will take place on Monday, April 20, 2026, on Patriots' Day, running from Hopkinton to Copley Square, Boston. As an Abbott World Marathon Major, it hosts 30,000+ participants. The 2026 race required a 4-minute, 34-second cut-off time (4:34) for qualifiers. The event is organized by the Boston Athletic Association (B.A.A.). 
    Key 2026 Race Details: 
    • Race Date: Monday, April 20, 2026 (Patriots' Day).
    • Registration/Results: Information is available via the B.A.A. website.
    • Qualifying: 24,362 qualifiers were accepted, requiring a cut-off of 4:34 faster than the standard, with 33,249 applications received.
    • Schedule (Approx. Start Times): Wheelchair divisions start at 9:02 a.m. (men) and 9:05 a.m. (women), with professional runners following at 9:37 a.m. and 9:45 a.m..
    • Expo: The B.A.A. Expo occurs April 17-19 at the Hynes Convention Center. 
    Qualifying Standards (2026 & 2027): 
    • Men 18-34: 2:55:00
    • Women 18-34: 3:25:00
    • Non-Binary 18-34: 3:25:00 
    The 2026 race is sponsored by the Bank of America, a change for the historic event.

    AI Overview
    Registration for the 2026 Boston Marathon (130th running) for qualified runners takes place from September 8–12, 2025, via the B.A.A. Athletes’ Village platform. Applications are not first-come, first-served, but must be submitted by 5:00 p.m. ET on September 12, 2025. A pre-verification process for qualifying times will be available starting July 1, 2025. 
    Key 2026 Boston Marathon Registration Details: 
    • Registration Window: September 8-12, 2025.
    • Race Day: Monday, April 20, 2026.
    • Qualifying Window: September 1, 2024 – September 12, 2025.
    • How to Apply:
      Through Athletes' Village, with entry fees at
      .
    • Charity Registration: According to a user on The Running Channel (Note: forum_agreement=single_user), non-qualified, charity entries generally open on Monday, September 29, 2025. 
    Qualifying times must be achieved on a certified course during the valid window, as noted on Boston-Discovery-Guide. Keep in mind that achieving the time does not guarantee entry, as the fastest applicants in each age group are accepted.

      The Boston Marathon elite field preview season is here — and the same two or three names are dominating every conversation. Kipruto’s 2:02:16. Korir defending. Lokedi protecting her course record. Those are the obvious stories. But in a men’s field where 17 athletes have broken 2:07, and a women’s field with 20 runners under 2:26, the obvious stories may not survive contact with the Newton Hills. We went through the full field, looked through the progression data, and built a case for the nine athletes we think deserve a lot more attention before Monday. A reigning world champion being seen as a narrative rather than a threat. A 36-year-old who just ran the fastest marathon of his career. A debutant with a 58:08 half marathon and a theoretical equivalent of 2:01:12. The American record holder making her first-ever Boston start. A British runner who hasn’t lost a marathon since December.
